headline: Russia's Laundry Bear drew a multinational government advisory for zero-click Zimbra webmail espionage as Check Point rushed a patch for an actively exploited firewall-management zero-day.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep hiding command-and-control inside the victim's own trusted software, from Chaos ransomware's msaRAT driving headless Chrome and Edge over WebRTC to a fake Claude installer served straight off the claude.ai domain, defeating network defenses that trust legitimate processes and hosts.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Chaos Ransomware Routes C2 Through the Victim's Browser

emerging_trends.text: Edge and management appliances remain the softest targets, with Check Point patching an actively exploited SmartConsole authentication bypass that hands attackers full firewall admin control, extending a run of exploited gateway and VPN flaws.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Check Point SmartConsole Zero-Day Exploited for Admin Takeover

emerging_trends.text: AI systems now sit on both sides of the fight, as OpenAI's AgentForger fix and a Claude Cowork sandbox escape show attackers forging invisible AI insiders and breaking agent containment even as new malware like Dolphin X uses AI to rank which victims to hit first.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Agents Draw Insider-Forgery and Sandbox-Escape Flaws

topics.title: Laundry Bear Zimbra Espionage Draws Joint International Advisory
topics.latest_developments: The NSA, CISA, and partner agencies published joint advisory AA26-204A on July 23, 2026, formally documenting the Russian state-supported group Laundry Bear compromising Western government and commercial organizations running Zimbra Collaboration Suite since at least July 2025, while Palo Alto's Unit 42 detailed the JavaScript injection and Dark Reading described the half-click emails that require a victim only to open or preview a message.
topics.summary: Laundry Bear, also tracked as Void Blizzard, exploits a now-patched Zimbra webmail flaw to lift the last 90 days of mail, the full organizational email directory, browser-saved passwords, and two-factor recovery codes from targets across the US and Ukraine. Zimbra administrators should apply the patch and hunt for the injected JavaScript.

sources.title: Russian State-Supported Cyber Actors Conduct Phishing Campaign Targeting Users of Zimbra Collaboration Suite
Russian Global Webmail Espionage
Russian Espionage Group Exploited Zimbra Zero-Day to Steal Mail and 2FA Codes
Russian Hackers Exploit Zimbra Zero-Day Against US, Ukraine Targets

topics.title: Check Point SmartConsole Zero-Day Exploited for Admin Takeover
topics.latest_developments: Check Point released updates for its Security Management and Multi-Domain Management products fixing CVE-2026-16232, a 9.3-rated authentication bypass in the SmartConsole login process that attackers already exploit in the wild against customers with certain configurations to obtain an application login token and log in with full admin rights.
topics.summary: The flaw lets an unauthenticated attacker seize the management servers that push policy to Check Point firewalls, then alter security policy and configuration. Administrators should patch immediately and review policy changes for tampering.

sources.title: New Check Point Zero-Day Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild
Check Point warns of SmartConsole zero-day exploited in attacks

topics.title: Chaos Ransomware Routes C2 Through the Victim's Browser
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos detailed msaRAT, a Rust implant it attributes to the Chaos ransomware group that never opens its own outbound connection but instead launches Chrome or Edge in headless mode, drives them through the Chrome DevTools Protocol, and tunnels command-and-control over a WebRTC channel that hides the attacker's IP from the victim.
topics.summary: Found on a compromised Windows machine ahead of the encryptor, msaRAT enables arbitrary command execution while its traffic blends into ordinary browser activity. Defenders should watch for unexpected headless browser processes and DevTools debugging activity.

sources.title: Chaos ransomware's msaRAT: Living off the browser to build a covert C2 channel
Chaos Ransomware Uses msaRAT to Route C2 Traffic Through Headless Chrome and Edge
New msaRAT malware uses Chrome, Edge browsers to route C2 traffic

topics.title: AI Agents Draw Insider-Forgery and Sandbox-Escape Flaws
topics.latest_developments: OpenAI fixed AgentForger, a ChatGPT Agent flaw that let an attacker create, insert, and remotely control an invisible autonomous AI agent inside a victim organization, while Accomplish AI disclosed a sandbox escape in Anthropic's Claude Cowork that lets the agent break out of its Linux virtual machine to read or write files anywhere on roughly 500,000 users' Macs, and BleepingComputer profiled Dolphin X, a remote access trojan that uses AI profiling to score and rank infected victims.
topics.summary: The disclosures show AI agents serving as both attack surface and attack tool, with forged AI insiders, escaped sandboxes, and malware that uses AI to prioritize high-value targets. Organizations deploying agentic AI should enforce least-privilege access, isolate agent execution, and monitor for unauthorized agent creation.

sources.title: OpenAI Fixes ChatGPT Agent Flaw That Could Let Attackers Forge an AI Insider
Claude Cowork Flaw Could Let AI Agent Escape Its VM and Access Mac Files
New Dolphin X malware uses AI to rank high-value targets

topics.title: Fake Claude Installer on Claude.ai Domain Delivers SectopRAT
topics.latest_developments: Huntress researchers disclosed that a threat actor abused Anthropic's Claude Artifacts feature to host a fake Claude desktop download on the genuine claude.ai domain, then promoted it through sponsored Bing ads that compromised employees at at least 29 organizations over two days in July, redirecting them to a spoofed site serving SectopRAT.
topics.summary: The campaign trades on the trust of a legitimate domain and a real search ad to slip a remote access trojan past users hunting for the Claude desktop app. Organizations should treat sponsored search results for software downloads with suspicion and verify vendor download pages directly.

sources.title: How attackers hosted a fake Claude download page on the claude.ai domain
Fake Claude app promoted by Bing ads pushes SectopRAT malware

topics.title: Iranian Hackers Target Siemens, Schneider, and Rockwell PLCs
topics.latest_developments: US federal agencies issued an updated advisory warning that Iranian hackers are targeting programmable logic controllers from Siemens, Schneider Electric, and Rockwell Automation, detailing the techniques the actors use against the industrial control systems that run critical infrastructure.
topics.summary: The advisory adds fresh technical detail on how Iranian operators reach and manipulate PLCs across critical manufacturing, energy, and water sectors. Operators should segment control networks, change default credentials, and restrict internet exposure of these devices.

sources.title: US Warns of Iranian Hackers Targeting Siemens, Schneider, and Rockwell ICS Devices

business_politics.title: AI Spending Fears Wipe $890 Billion Off Big Tech
business_politics.latest_developments: Earnings from Alphabet and Tesla reignited fears that hyperscalers are overspending on AI, and the Magnificent Seven shed roughly $890 billion in market value Thursday, deepening a broad selloff.
business_politics.summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply July 23 as investors dumped technology shares over runaway AI data-center spending; Tesla dropped about 15% on a weak quarter, the slide compounded a rout in chip stocks, and it landed atop a jump in oil and Treasury yields, denting the trade that has carried the market.

business_politics.title: Trump Rebuilds Tariff Wall on 60 Countries
business_politics.latest_developments: Trump imposed new double-digit tariffs on 60 trading partners July 23 as his stopgap 10% levies expire Friday, pinning them to a forced-labor probe to survive the legal challenges that sank his blanket levies at the Supreme Court.
business_politics.summary: After the Supreme Court struck down his across-the-board tariffs, President Trump rebuilt the wall with country-by-country duties tied to a forced-labor investigation, hitting dozens of nations and structuring the measures to withstand court review, reshaping U.S. trade policy.
